title: Algorithm Design and Physician Liability
abstract: arXiv:2608.13618v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: A single clinical algorithm can deliver unequal accuracy across patient groups, and concern about such disparity has grown as artificial intelligence (AI) spreads through clinical decision-making. In response, a liability rule introduced in the United States holds healthcare providers responsible when their reliance on disparate algorithms contributes to erroneous clinical decisions. We examine how such liability considerations reshape (i) an AI firm's algorithm design decisions that drive group-specific accuracy and (ii) a physician's decisions to use AI in healthcare delivery. The AI firm designs an algorithm for two patient groups, and improving accuracy for the disadvantaged group is more costly. translated_abstract: 摘要：单一的临床算法在不同患者群体间可能产生不均衡的准确性，随着人工智能（AI）在临床决策中的普及，这种差异引发的担忧日益增长。为此，美国引入了一项责任规则，规定当医疗服务提供者依赖有差异的算法导致错误临床决策时，需承担责任。我们研究了此类责任考量如何重塑（i）AI公司的算法设计决策（这些决策决定群体特定准确性）以及（ii）医生在医疗服务中使用AI的决策。AI公司为两个患者群体设计算法，提高弱势群体准确性的成本更高。医生（作为最终负责的决策者）随后决定是否咨询AI，权衡临床不确定性的减少与AI错误不成比例地影响弱势群体时预期的责任风险。
tldr: 本文研究了美国责任规则如何影响AI公司的算法设计（针对不同患者群体的准确性权衡）和医生的AI使用决策，揭示责任考量在平衡临床效益与群体差异风险中的关键作用。
en_tdlr: This paper examines how U.S. liability rules reshape AI firms' algorithm design (accuracy trade-offs across patient groups) and physicians' AI adoption decisions, highlighting the critical role of liability considerations in balancing clinical benefits against group disparity risks.
